kitDescription: Snow Crane is a Water SR Defender whose kit is entirely sustain and team protection, with no damage lines of her own. Her Skill 1 passively raises all allies' Max HP by 10% of her own Max HP, but only while she is not in Terminated Contract status; when she receives healing from another unit she stacks Proof of Violation, which weakens her outgoing healing, up to three stacks. Her Skill 2 heals the team a small amount after every third full-charge shot (targeting allies still under her Exclusive Recovery Agreement), and puts a 10-second shield worth 9.5% of her Max HP on all allies every time the team enters Full Burst. Once Proof of Violation reaches max stacks she flips into Terminated Contract: immune to further stacks and regenerating a small amount of HP every second, while her team Max HP grant switches off. Her burst heals all allies for 44.68% of her Max HP and grants herself Pierce for 10 seconds. In the sim her footprint is the recovery/shield event cadence (which drives teammates' on-recovery and on-shield triggers) plus the timed self-Pierce window; the healing magnitudes and the Proof-of-Violation cascade are unmodeled because the engine has no HP pool and no heal-source filter.

faithfulnessScore: 1.0 (7/7 kit lines: 5 FAITHFUL — S1a grant, S2a charge-heal, S2b FB-entry shield, burst heal, burst Pierce — and 2 DOCUMENTED_GAP — Proof of Violation, Terminated Contract — both verbatim in unmodeled with reasons and a recipe; the two partial-clause elisions, S1a's Terminated-Contract off-gate and S2a's ERA-membership target filter, are documented in caveats and offensively inert)
verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHA found: every divergence between the shipped override and the prose is documented, and the two fully unmodeled lines are carried verbatim with an inexpressibility argument (no heal-source filter, no outgoing-healing StatKey, no self-status channel) that all three independent agents reached separately. The blind re-derivations converged on all five core encodings; the two S6 divergences were ruled spurious and actively worse — the always-on Terminated-Contract regen would fabricate a 1Hz recovery-event stream that is damage-BEARING through tandem consumers (asuka/crown) in comps where the real kit emits nothing, and the omitted countInFb would trip the chargeCounter primitive's SBS-baked ?? 1 default and over-fire the S2a heal for 10s after every own cast (the driver authored countInFb:3 explicitly and pinned both directions with counterfactuals — the strongest single catch in this packet). The raw S5 REDs were fixture-premises, not spec divergences — controlComp's crown wins every stage-II cast so snow-crane never bursts there (S2b's own predicted hazard), the comp is 4 units, an illegal empty-effects strip, and crown being a recovery consumer — and the documented A1-A4 adaptation runs 17/0-fail with the 3 skips being the blind model's own declared GAPs. Discrimination is real throughout: M2's floor(charges/3)+casts equality, M3's every-FB-vs-zero shield-gate split under the two-B2 fixture, and M5's no-tag < 10s-window < permanent pierce inequality chain each fail under their named nearest-wrong model. Same-model residuals for the owner to spot-check: (1) the countInFb-default claim is an engine-semantics reading of sim.ts firePull that every agent here sourced the same way — worth one direct glance at the primitive; (2) the burstCast-vs-fullBurstEnter split rests on prose that is explicit for the shield and on the no-activation-clause convention for the burst lines — low risk, but it is the kit's one deliberate trigger-identity asymmetry; (3) heal-magnitude inertness assumes no shipped or future consumer reads heal amounts (true in v1: no HP pool).
